sentences.text:
The claimant has preferred this appeal being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award dated 03.09.2010 passed in M.V.C. No. 2952/2008 on the file of the learned Prl. Sr. Civil Judge & MACT,
Belgaum (hereinafter referred to as the Tribunal), awarding compensation of Rs.58,900/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation.
Parties shall be referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.
2. Brief facts of the case are that the claimant filed claim petition claiming compensation for the injuries suffered by him.

It is stated that he was traveling in the Canter bearing reg. no.
MH-09/BC-9099 which was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the stationed truck bearing reg. no. KA-02/AB-7607 as a result of which the claimant sustained injuries.
He was shifted to General Hospital, Nelamangala and he took treatment as an inpatient from 28.07.2007 to 14.08.2007.
Later he was shifted to a private hospital at Nippani and he took treatment as inpatient.
It is stated that the claimant was aged 36 years at the time of accident and he was working as a Driver.
He suffered permanent disability and therefore he is entitled for compensation.
Respondent No.1 insured of the Canter bearing reg. no. MH-09/BC-9099 has not contested the matter.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle filed objection statement denying the contentions of the claimant and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.

3. On the basis of these pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that the alleged accident in question was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the Canter bearing reg. no. MH-09/BC-9099 by its driver and the petitioner sustained injuries as alleged?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, for what amount and from whom?
3. What award or order?
4. The claimant himself examined as PW1 and got marked documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.12 in support of his contention.

sentences.text: The insurer-respondent did not lead any evidence.
The Tribunal after considering all these materials on record came to the conclusion that the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.58,900/- with interest at 6% p.a.
Being aggrieved by the same, the claimant has preferred this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

5. Heard Sri Harish S. Maigur, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri M.K. Soudagar, learned counsel for insurer- respondent.
6.
Learned counsel for the appellant contends that the injured had suffered grievous injuries and was hospitalized for a period of 23 days.
The accident had occurred during the year 2007.
The Tribunal has not taken into consideration the income of the claimant at that point of time nor it had considered the disability suffered by the claimant.
Learned counsel submitted that even though medical records are not produced by the claimant, Ex.P.10 is the photograph which clearly shows that the claimant has suffered permanent disability.
Hence, he prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the compensation.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 opposing the appeal submitted that as per the wound certificate the claimant has suffered only two simple injuries and therefore there was no question of hospitalization of the claimant nor there is any chance of suffering permanent disability.
The Tribunal after taking into consideration all the materials on record arrived at a right conclusion and thus the impugned judgment does not call for interference.

Hence, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.
8.
Perused the material on record including the trial Court records.

9. The point that arises for consideration in this appeal is:
Whether the impugned judgment and award calls for interference?

10. My answer to the above point is in the negative for the following:
REASONS 11.
It is the specific contention of the claimant that he has suffered injuries which resulted in disability and he took treatment for a prolonged period.
Even though such pleadings are found in the claim petition, the claimant produced Ex.P.5 according to which he has suffered two simple injuries, i.e., local tenderness.
Ex.P.6 is dated 05.06.2008 issued by the Private Hospital at Nippani which refers to some old infection.
The date of accident is 28.07.2007.
Between the date of accident till 15.09.2007 on which the claimant said to have admitted to the private hospital, there are no medical records.
Strangely claimant also has not examined the Doctor who treated him.
No disability certificate is produced on behalf of the claimant.
Under such circumstances, I do not find any merit in the contention taken by the claimant.

sentences.text: I have gone through the impugned judgment passed by the Tribunal.
It has taken into consideration all the materials that are placed before it and awarded just compensation.
I do not find any reason to interfere with the same.
Hence, I proceed to pass the following order.
ORDER Appeal filed by the appellant-claimant is dismissed with costs.
Consequently, impugned judgment and award dated 03.09.2010 passed in M.V.C. No. 2952/2008 on the file of the learned Prl. Sr. Civil Judge & MACT, Belgaum, is confirmed.
Send back the trial Court records.

SD/-
